title: Gate jobs and slots follow the machine's free capacity
what: Design when taken: whether the gate's slot count, its test job count or the precheck's jobs should follow free capacity (load, free cores), with at least two approaches plus do nothing, measured on live gates; related: waiting-gates-take-a-free-slot-in-no-order.
why: 29 Oct 09:55 measured: 12 cores; load 8.6 rose to 32.7 in four minutes while one precheck and one pytest run ran beside 5 other lanes' gates and 8 test worker processes. Driver: gate slots x RELAY_TEST_JOBS x lanes' own precheck runs add up with no look at free capacity. The item tests-with-a-fixed-time-limit-fail-on-a-loaded-m asked whether jobs or slots should depend on free capacity; its fix raised every fixed wait to a 600 s hang bound and left this decision open.

fact: 29 Oct afternoon, metrics worker: load average 34 on the 12-core Mac with 6 lanes plus the podman machine (10 CPUs, 20 GiB); the full library suite did not finish in 35 min and the precheck's changed-tests step (old 230 s cap, still on that branch) went red from load alone.

29 Oct ~15:30, front, measured with sysctl, ps, top, vm_stat: load 27-31 on 12 cores (8 performance, 4 efficiency). Process limit not near: 392 processes of the user's limit 5333 (564 of 8000 on the machine). Memory is the bottleneck: 32 GB Mac, 152 MB unused, compressor 14 GB, swap 6.4 of 7 GB, CPU 74% system, 26% user, 0% idle. The podman machine (applehv, 10 CPUs, 20 GiB) holds 20 GB plus 24 GB compressed while idle, with no container running: applehv returns no guest memory until the machine stops. fseventsd holds 6.9 GB (file events from test churn).

question: **Сколько памяти отдать podman на Mac с 32 GB**
Машина podman держит 20 GB из 32 и не отдаёт их, пока её не остановить; без контейнеров она простаивает, а Mac тратит 74% процессора на сжатие памяти и swap.
options: a. Уменьшить до 8 GiB и 6 ядер, перезапустить сейчас (контейнеров нет)
b. Оставить 20 GiB, но останавливать машину между запусками контейнеров
reading: Shrink the podman machine to 8 GiB and 6 CPUs and restart it now.

fact: 29 Oct afternoon, front: relay precheck's changed-tests step went red on its 600 s limit three times in 3 hours, on three branches (metrics, landed-branch item, gates-and-tests sweep), with no test failing; load 36-50 on 12 cores, CPU 38-24% user, 62-76% system, 0% idle. At ~16:30 the test processes were 7 in the metrics worktree, 7 in the landed-branch worktree, 1 landing train, 6 in temp test folders, while 2 gate slots were busy: prechecks take no gate slot, and every precheck and gate sizes its workers for the whole machine. Front decision (owner can reverse): this item takes the next free lane, ahead of the container gate, because the same failure repeated (principle 6) and every rerun is waste (principle 2).

29 Oct, front, correction to the note of ~16:30: that prechecks take no gate slot and that each run sizes its workers for the whole machine is a front assumption, not measured; the build measures it first.

29 Oct, design revision 2 (thinker, critic, revision) from 608 gate logs of 27-29 Oct: a second gate at once added only 5-20% more gates per hour; median library-test time of a gate running alone 404 s. Modelled under the afternoon load (2 gates plus 5 agents' test runs): a pool of 12 tokens with 4 kept per gate gives about 808 s per gate (a 5th agent's run waits); 12 with 2 per gate about 923 s (no agent waits); 8 with 2 per gate about 1616 s, at the 30-min limit. Critic: nested token takes deadlock unless a child runs on its parent's token (fixed in revision 2). Not measured: slowdown at 12 processes, how often 5+ agent runs coincide.
